findings.summary: plan cache can serve a stale parse after a non-atomic plan write
findings.text: reckon/crew/section_obligations.py:109: the plan-cache fast path returns the stored parse whenever the plan's directory identity matches and never stats the plan file itself, so a plan written in place (no entry added, removed or renamed in its directory) stays stale for the process's lifetime; document the atomic-write assumption as a requirement on writers or revalidate the plan file on the same cadence the sweep uses.

findings.summary: third spelling of directory stat identity
findings.text: reckon/crew/section_obligations.py:33: the module adds a third spelling of a directory's stat identity, beside recovery_memo.py:533 _directory_identity and review_records.py:1519 _store_directory_identity, which already own that question; the recursive map is new but the per-directory identity it builds should compose the existing owner rather than restate the stat fields.

findings.summary: review-record case's publish assertion is satisfied by the floor tick
findings.text: tests/test_an_unchanged_sweep_reads_no_plan_and_walks_no_tree.py:379: the review-record case asserts only that the sweep wrote something, and the fixture advances the clock 180 s past a 60 s floor tick, so that assertion is satisfied by the floor tick whatever the review record does; the case's real claim -- that the new record reaches the published obligations -- rests entirely on the cold-sweep equality on line 382, which would also hold if both arms read a stale review index.

findings.summary: dead pop with the wrong key leaves a superseded parse behind
findings.text: reckon/crew/section_obligations.py:115: store.reads.pop(plan, None) keys the caches by plan slug, but every write into store.reads uses str(path), so this pop removes nothing and a superseded parse is left in the map when a plan's file can no longer be resolved.
